idea-plugin.name: Window Tabs
idea-plugin.description:
Every open project becomes a tab at the top of each IDE window, like the native window tabs JetBrains IDEs offer on macOS. Built for Linux, where that feature does not exist.

  • Click a tab to switch: that project's window takes the current window's size and position (or stays maximized) and comes to the front.
  • Middle-click, or the × shown on hover, closes the project.
  • + opens another project.
  • While the IDE reopens the last session, projects still loading show as dimmed tabs.
  • Alt+Shift+1…9 jump to a tab; Window | Project Tabs also has next and previous tab, ready for a shortcut of your choice.
  • Drag a tab to reorder the strip; the order is kept for the next start.
  • Each tab shows the project's icon. With many projects the tabs keep a readable width and the strip scrolls.

Each project stays in its own window, so the IDE handles projects exactly as before. Works in every JetBrains IDE 2024.3 or newer, Android Studio included. Settings | Appearance & Behavior | Window Tabs shows the strip with a single project, hides the icons, or turns the strip on for macOS, where it is off by default because macOS has native window tabs.

GNOME on Wayland: if GNOME shows a "ready" notice instead of raising the window, run the IDE on X11: Help → Edit Custom VM Options → -Dawt.toolkit.name=XToolkit.
